Issues.Title: Make test-quarantine evidence collection deterministic
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Fix the upstream reliability gaps behind test-quarantine runs [169](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/40486887980) and [168](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/40183792842). Their fail-closed `report_incomplete` conclusions were correct; this preserves those semantics rather than hiding incomplete analysis.

- Verify each exact historical Case B tracking issue in authenticated, trusted pre-activation code. Cache the lookup, accept open or closed issues, reject pull requests/mismatches, retry transient errors, and require `case_b_issue_verified` when validating a re-quarantine patch. The agent no longer needs to repeat existence confirmation through integrity-filtered MCP reads or its failing TLS fallback.
- Collect all 30 days of main-branch completed builds and paginated test results for pipelines 84 and 87 before activation. Resolve source targets with the existing parser and history helpers; preserve exact theory rows and separate pipeline denominators. Produce compact candidates and collection counts so the agent cannot skip raw Part 2 collection to conserve its turn budget.
- Require complete, identity-bound Part 2 evidence, including the history receipt's SHA-256, before privileged output processing. Removals must match an exact eligible source target and issue, in addition to the existing first-quarantine and patch checks.

The collector retains the 60-day age, zero-failure/real-pass, 66% build-appearance, re-quarantine, human suppression, sentinel, and source exclusion gates. Class/assembly checks include combined attribute lists, and suppression matching does not merge unrelated classes sharing a method name. Uncertain re-quarantine ownership for the same issue/file remains conservative; truncated diffs block the whole file.

## Validation

- Existing source/history collector fixtures.
- 17 new collector/issue-verification tests covering pagination, failed collection, empty-but-complete results, per-pipeline denominators, skips/failures/age/appearance, exact theory rows, class/assembly completeness, IIS variants, suppression, re-quarantine PR scope, and receipt-backed removals.
- Existing pull-request patch validator fixtures, with new missing/incomplete/hash-mismatched Part 2 cases.
- Existing workflow policy and JavaScript KBE handler fixtures.
- Baseline-versus-patched checks at the actual patch boundary: the old validator accepts unverified Case B issue reuse and an unquarantine patch without passing evidence; the patched validator rejects both.
- Regression cases reproduced the review findings before correction and passed afterward.
- Live, read-only Azure DevOps payload smoke checks for both pipelines.
- Strict compilation and lockfile regeneration with the existing gh-aw v0.92.0 toolchain. The lockfile was generated, not manually edited.

Two independent reviewers examined the implementation, then approved the corrected findings in follow-up review.

## Boundary

No live quarantine outputs or repository variables were changed. A complete scheduled/staged Actions run is not exercised locally; CI and the first post-merge run still need to validate end-to-end operation. Pre-activation now does the Part 2 API work and one additional source-index scan, so its runtime should be monitored.

Issues.Title: [release/10.0] Remove temporary Pkcs references after Microsoft.Identity.Web dependency update
Issues.Body:
## Background

PR #70038 needs temporary explicit `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 9.0.21 references in the Identity.Web-enabled project templates to avoid NU1902/NU1903 restore failures under .NET 10 transitive NuGet auditing and warnings-as-errors.

The current dependency chain is `Microsoft.Identity.Web` 3.15.1 → `Microsoft.Identity.Web.TokenCache` 3.15.1 → `System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs` 9.0.15. The latest published Identity.Web 3.x version, 3.16.0, still requests Pkcs 9.0.18. The upstream dependency update to Pkcs 9.0.21 merged in https://github.com/AzureAD/microsoft-identity-web/pull/4098 but is not yet available in a published 3.x package.

Diagnosis: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70038#issuecomment-6438434842

## Cleanup

Once a compatible Microsoft.Identity.Web 3.x package is published with a non-vulnerable Pkcs dependency (9.0.21 or later):

- Update the Identity.Web dependencies on release/10.0.
- Remove the temporary explicit Pkcs references from `src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/StarterWeb-CSharp.csproj.in`, `RazorPagesWeb-CSharp.csproj.in`, and `WebApi-CSharp.csproj.in`.
- Verify SingleOrg and IndividualB2C MVC, Razor Pages, and Web API template restores/builds/publishes pass with transitive auditing and warnings-as-errors, without the explicit references or diagnostic suppression.

Do not remove the workaround solely because a new Identity.Web version is available: verify its resolved Pkcs dependency is patched. Unlike .NET 11, Pkcs is not part of the .NET 10 ASP.NET Core targeting pack and cannot simply be pruned.

Reject invalid HPACK index 0 before invoking the header handler.

## Description

RFC 7541 section 6.1 requires index 0 in an indexed header field to be treated as a decoding error. The decoder previously forwarded it to the header handler, where the static-table lookup threw IndexOutOfRangeException. Reject it with HPackDecodingException and the existing invalid-index message instead.

Adds a zero-index regression test and valid HPACK static-table boundary coverage. Also adds QPACK boundary tests for indexed fields and name references: unlike HPACK, QPACK uses zero-based indexes, so index 0 remains valid. HPACK literal-name marker 0 is unchanged.

Project frozen review inputs for reliable native reads

## Description

This projects GitHub review data into a compact frozen bundle, removes duplicate `files[].patch`, externalizes multiline required text as integrity-checked `.source` files, and gives each routed guide a disjoint exact-file assignment. The latest replacement aligns worker consumption with the evaluator contract: workers trust producer/checker-validated assignment metadata, read every assigned non-source file to EOF through native `view`/`read_file`, never invoke `bash`, `shell`, or `powershell`, and use native search only beneath assigned frozen source roots.

The complete coordinator bundle, frozen target identities, independent adjudication, source roles, routing provenance, tamper/reuse checks, diff reconstruction, and explicit `BLOCKED` failures remain intact. This does not add trace parsing, a sandbox, worker receipts, generalized chunking, or a second live-read architecture; #70055 continues to own post-read native trace grading.

<details>
<summary>Stable bundle and worker contract</summary>

- `diff.patch` is authoritative; projected `files.json` contains changed-file metadata without duplicate patches.
- Pull/feedback/policy/exclusion bodies are inert `.source` files referenced by bundle-relative path, UTF-8 byte length, and SHA-256.
- Each `guides[].assignment.files[]` entry is exactly `{ kind, path, utf8Bytes, sha256 }`; `assignment.sourceRoles[]` names only assigned frozen source roles.
- The coordinator supplies the trusted absolute bundle root, verbatim assignment, frozen target identities, and only `sources[role].root` mappings for assigned roles.
- Workers do not recompute assignment lengths or hashes. They read each assigned non-source file to EOF with native `view`/`read_file`, paging with `view_range` or equivalent offset/limit until the final line; truncation is a required-input failure.
- Workers never use `bash`, `shell`, or `powershell`. Native `rg`/`grep`/`glob` is permitted only beneath assigned frozen source roots.
- Parent/shared bundle enumeration, sibling inference, unassigned paths, and intermediate output derived from those scopes remain prohibited.
- Per-guide policies and exclusions are physically projected beneath disjoint `required/guides/<guide-index>/...` paths.
- The hosted `/review` dispatch passes references rather than duplicated inline guide/policy/exclusion/diff/changed-file contents.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Compatibility and bounded unresolved behavior</summary>

- The projected bundle shape changes under manifest v2. Acceptance is revision-bound by the exact producer SHA, so an older same-version bundle is rejected before shape validation; no independent in-repo compatibility consumer was found. Out-of-repo consumers are unknown.
- The 2,048-byte serialized/required-text line limit is a conservative producer fail-closed bound derived from retained long-line native-reader failures, not a measured platform cutoff. At 2,048 bytes preparation succeeds; at 2,049 bytes it fails before writing a manifest.
- `diff.patch` and routed guide `.source` long-line behavior remains an unresolved, unverified boundary and is not redesigned here.
- Closed or merged PR review is intentionally unsupported; all supported workflow entry points require the frozen PR state to be open.
- Required text is not deterministically wrapped or chunked because inserting newlines can change Markdown, code, table, link, or HTML semantics.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Deterministic red/green and validation evidence</summary>

Red-before focused controls failed for the expected missing contract clauses before each correction: native exact-file/no-shell wording, paging-to-final-line behavior, and the retained native-local-coordinator `--allow-all-paths` prohibition.

Green results:

- Focused worker-contract test: 1/1 passed, 0 failed/skipped.
- Complete deterministic suite: 90/90 passed, 0 failed/skipped.
- Full command: `. .\activate.ps1; dotnet run --project .github\skills\review-pull-request\scripts\PrepareReview.Tests.csproj -- -preEnumerateTheories -reporter quiet`.
- Skill validation passed.
- Verified gh-aw v0.92.0 compile passed for `pull-request-review`.
- Strict workflow validation passed with `validate pull-request-review --strict --no-check-update`.
- Generated workflow lock drift is only `body_hash`: `9fd5253a988aaa0f297951b838de12517d98fe7fd76fbb6a37bc69d0cdb527ac` → `3a4a75250d3317d54068adee130964598b1822736157c6d95a0db7eca13c941a`.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Retained reports:

- `worker-native-read-coordinator-guard-focused.xml`
- `worker-native-read-coordinator-guard-full.xml`

</details>

<details>
<summary>Immutable replacement evidence and independent review</summary>

- Head: `68fa968990de2e6e991e75fd8debceb26fe3cf62`
- Tree: `9ee702a5ed0b150e950207247a70ba62b35540b4`
- Parent: `71b0131d7b170e1279f1a936946fc13cbec45eac`
- Replacement patch SHA-256: `f295645bf5d73afb014236f732aa52fff0925fe24ab46f1ea48b4402fefdef50`
- Replacement diff: four files, `+78/-23`.
- GPT-5.6 Sol: approved with no significant issues.
- Gemini 4 Argon: approved with no significant issues.
- Claude Haiku 5.5: no blocking issues; two low-level wording suggestions were adjudicated as already covered by the assignment definition and retained native-read/coordinator-denial rules, so the frozen patch was not changed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>#70055 migration contract</summary>

- Consume `guides[].assignment.files[]` exactly as `{ kind, path, utf8Bytes, sha256 }` and `guides[].assignment.sourceRoles[]` as frozen source-role names.
- Treat assignment length/hash values as producer/checker trust metadata; do not require worker-side recomputation.
- Expect exact native reads of every assigned non-source file through EOF, with paging to the final line and truncation treated as incomplete.
- Reject worker `bash`, `shell`, and `powershell` calls.
- Permit native search only beneath the assigned `sources[role].root` values.
- Grade parent/broad bundle reads, sibling/unassigned paths, and contaminated intermediate outputs fail-closed without worker-authored receipts.
- Expect coordinator exclusions under `required/coordinator/exclusions/...`, guide policies under `required/guides/<guide-index>/policies/...`, and guide-specific exclusion copies under `required/guides/<guide-index>/exclusions/...`.

</details>

Fixes the native-reader transport failure observed while reviewing #69782.

# Modernize process management with .NET 11 APIs

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).

- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [ ] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Fix process hangs and cleanup bugs, and reduce process-management overhead.

## Description

This PR uses .NET 11 process APIs to improve the reliability and efficiency of ASP.NET Core's tooling, test infrastructure, and process-launching code. It is not just an API modernization: it addresses existing deadlock risks, resource leaks, and child-process lifetime problems.

### Reliability and bug fixes

- **Avoid output-pipe deadlocks.** Drain stdout and stderr concurrently rather than reading one before the other, leaving redirected stderr unread, or waiting for exit before draining output. These bugs affected the review-helper tests, package integration tests, AppVerifier, and the shared process helper. See the [AppVerifier explanation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70076#discussion_r4401096364).
- **Distinguish process exit from output EOF.** Exit-status waits avoid waiting for descendant processes that keep redirected pipes open after the launched process exits. Conversely, the HTTP.sys tests now explicitly wait for exit after reading output: closing stdout does not mean the command has finished. See the [exit-versus-EOF explanation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70076#discussion_r4400934874).
- **Release resources and clean up child processes.** Dispose previously unreleased `Process` wrappers, including the monitored parent process. Use atomic Windows parent-exit cleanup for the IIS Express process tree, covering graceful exit, forced termination, and crashes. Kill timed-out Docker commands rather than merely disposing their wrappers, which does not terminate them. See the [IIS Express lifetime explanation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70076#discussion_r4401109227).
- **Make failure handling explicit.** Avoid exception-based lookup when the monitored parent has already exited, act on the nginx startup timeout, log the previously ignored nginx shutdown timeout, and replace a synchronous wait in asynchronous IIS Express cleanup.

### Efficiency and maintainability

- **Reduce custom output-processing overhead.** Built-in capture and line-reading APIs replace manual event handlers, buffers, background tasks, and locking where live callbacks are unnecessary. Gateway tool installation no longer starts two background tasks or needs locks; project-ID resolution also uses built-in capture. Crankier discards unused stderr directly instead of creating an unread pipe. These are implementation-level reductions, not benchmarked speedup claims.
- **Improve process-launch concurrency and trimming opportunities.** Explicit inherited-handle lists limit inheritance to the intended standard handles and allow parallel process creation on Windows. Leaving the modern `UseShellExecute = false` default unset also allows NativeAOT to eliminate shell-execution code where applicable; no binary-size measurement is claimed. See the [handle-inheritance explanation](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/70076#discussion_r4400868730).
- **Remove unnecessary subprocesses and helpers.** Use `Environment.UserName` instead of launching `whoami`, send SIGTERM with `Process.Signal` instead of spawning `kill`, and delete the unused OpenAPI test `ProcessEx` wrapper.

Live logging and readiness protocols retain event-based handling where needed, and older-target compatibility paths remain. The SPA shutdown-script check still has its existing timing race; porting the API does not fix that. The nginx shutdown timeout is now reported, but whether to kill that command remains an open review question.

### Testing the skill

This PR is also a real-world test of the `process-api-net11` skill being developed in [dotnet/skills#1322](https://github.com/dotnet/skills/pull/1322). We are testing its guidance against ASP.NET Core's existing code, with human review of the generated changes. The inline review comments explain the motivation, bugs addressed, and remaining limitations, providing practical feedback on the skill rather than a claim that every generated change is correct or fully validated.

No shipping public API changes.

### Validation

`git diff --check 766e22542b..origin/modernize-process-apis` passed for the pushed changes.

Earlier implementation validation included focused builds and tests plus real-child-process checks for output pipe saturation and cancellation. These were not rerun against the final pushed revision during PR creation; they should not be read as a full validation of this revision. Full cross-platform and browser E2E validation has not been completed.

Issues.Title: [API Proposal] Restore server navigation when the last interactive Router is removed
Issues.Body: ## Background and Motivation Originating issue: #50069 An interactive `Router` enables browser navigation interception so that internal link clicks can be handled through interactive routing. When that router is dynamically removed, interception remains enabled. Subsequent clicks update the address bar but leave the previous page content visible because server-side navigation does not take over. ## Current Behavior - Rendering an interactive router enables navigation interception. - Disposing of the router does not disable browser-side interception. - Navigation can change the URL without updating the page. ## Expected Behavior - Interactive routers retain interception while active. - Removing one router does not disable interception for another active router sharing the same interception service. - Removing the last router releases interception, allowing server-side navigation to resume. - Reinserting a router restores interactive routing. ## Proposed Change - Add `DisableNavigationInterceptionAsync()` to `INavigationInterception`. - Make `Router` implement `IAsyncDisposable` while retaining `IDisposable`. - Coordinate interception ownership across built-in router instances. - Support disabling interception for Server and WebAssembly while preserving the existing renderer-ownership restriction. This proposal introduces a public API change through the new interface member and the additional interface implemented by `Router`. ## Usage Example An interactive component can conditionally render a router: ```razor @if (_showRouter) { } Go to Weather @code { private bool _showRouter = true; } ``` After removing the last interactive router, clicking **Go to Weather** should load the destination through server-side navigation. Applications using the built-in router would not need to call the new method directly. The framework would manage interception according to the router's lifetime. Host implementations of `INavigationInterception` would override the new operation to release browser-side interception. ## Proposed API ```diff namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Routing { public interface INavigationInterception { Task EnableNavigationInterceptionAsync(); + Task DisableNavigationInterceptionAsync(); } - public partial class Router : IComponent, - IHandleAfterRender, - IDisposable + public partial class Router : IComponent, + IHandleAfterRender, + IDisposable, + IAsyncDisposable { + ValueTask DisposeAsync(); } } ``` ## Proposed Contract - `DisableNavigationInterceptionAsync()` would have a default implementation that returns `Task.CompletedTask`, preserving compatibility with existing interface implementations. - Existing custom implementations would need to override it to provide actual disabling behavior. - Built-in routers sharing the same interception service would coordinate ownership. - The first active registration would enable interception, and releasing the last registration would disable it. - Routers sharing a pending enable operation would observe its outcome. - Renderer-managed asynchronous disposal would await cleanup. - Synchronous disposal would remain non-blocking, with deferred failures reported through the renderer or logging. - Disabling interception would clear browser-routing ownership only for the matching renderer. - Simultaneous routing ownership by different interactive runtimes would remain unsupported. ## Decisions Requested 1. Is a default no-op implementation the appropriate compatibility behavior? 2. Should `Router` implement `IAsyncDisposable` while retaining synchronous disposal? 3. Is service-keyed ownership coordination the appropriate lifetime boundary? 4. Should disabling remain parameterless to match the existing enable operation, or should it support cancellation? If cancellation is supported, what should happen to incomplete cleanup? 5. What ownership guarantees should apply when consumers call the interception service directly alongside built-in routers? ## Alternative Designs ### Disable Interception Whenever Any Router Is Disposed This approach is simpler but would prematurely disable interception when another router remains active. The proposed design releases interception only after the last built-in registration is removed. ### Reference-Count Every Public Enable Call This approach would turn repeated enable calls into ownership acquisitions and require corresponding releases. The proposed design keeps registration counting within built-in router lifetime management rather than changing the meaning of existing enable calls. ### Introduce a Public Registration Object A registration object could explicitly represent interception ownership and release. This would provide a more explicit ownership contract but would introduce additional public API surface. The proposed design instead extends the existing service with a disable operation. ## Risks - **Default implementation:** Existing custom implementations would remain compatible but would not automatically gain disabling behavior. - **Disposal behavior:** Adding `IAsyncDisposable` changes the disposal path selected by the renderer. - **Lifetime coordination:** Concurrent routers, pending enable operations, failures, and reinsertion must not corrupt ownership bookkeeping. - **Cleanup failures:** Unexpected failures must remain observable, while expected Server disconnection cleanup is handled appropriately. - **Mixed ownership:** Direct service callers and built-in router registrations need an explicitly defined ownership contract. - **Host differences:** Static SSR, Server, WebAssembly, Auto, and WebView have different activation and cleanup behaviors. ## Validation Expectations Coverage should establish that: - Removing the last router restores destination-page content, not merely the URL. - Removing one of multiple active routers preserves interactive routing. - Reinsertion restores interception. - Server, WebAssembly, and cold/warm Auto activation follow the same ownership contract. - Sequential runtime switching does not leave stale interception ownership. - Pending or failed enable operations release registrations correctly. -nup failures remain observable. ## Source Justification - **Problem:** "Each navigation updates the address bar without changing any content on the page." - dotnet/aspnetcore#50069. - **Expected fallback:** "Disabling navigation interception when the router gets removed would allow server-side routing to work again." - dotnet/aspnetcore#50069. - **Historical exploration:** The originating issue references dotnet/aspnetcore#50012 and dotnet/aspnetcore#50564. These provide historical context and should not be interpreted as approval of this proposal's API or lifetime contract.

Issues.Title: QuickGrid does not call stop when disposed while init is pending
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

This is a small follow-up to #47173, and it may not matter in practice.

The fix for #47173 (#62840) checks `_wasDisposed` after the module `import`. There is no such check after `init`. If `QuickGrid` is disposed while the `init` call is pending, `_jsEventDisposable` is still `null` at that time, so `DisposeAsync` does not call `stop`. The `click`, `mousedown`, and `keydown` listeners that `init` added then stay on `document.body`.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477/src/Components/QuickGrid/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.QuickGrid/src/QuickGrid.razor.cs#L314-L321

To be honest, I am not sure this happens in real apps. The window is only one JS interop round trip, so a user would rarely navigate away at exactly that moment. If you think it is not worth fixing, please feel free to close this.

### Expected Behavior

When `QuickGrid` is disposed, `stop` is called, even if `init` was still pending.

### Steps To Reproduce

The repro project is at https://github.com/jsakamotoIGJP/quickgrid-dispose-race-repro

It uses a Playwright script that delays the reply of `init` on purpose (the original `init` runs unchanged), because the real window is too short to hit by hand. With QuickGrid 10.0.14, leaving the page while the `init` reply is delayed leaves 3 listeners on `document.body`, and `stop` is not called.

### Exceptions (if any)

None.

### .NET Version

10.0.14 (QuickGrid package). The code is the same on `main`.

### Anything else?

The fix is small. It checks `_wasDisposed` once more after `init`, and calls `stop` if the grid has been disposed. I will open a PR, just in case it is worth taking.

Issues.Title: Identity UI and Blazor Identity pages return 500 for a malformed reset or confirmation code (unhandled FormatException)
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Hi! The password reset and email confirmation pages decode the `code` query string value with `WebEncoders.Base64UrlDecode` but don't handle `FormatException`. If the code in the link isn't valid Base64Url, the request fails with a 500 instead of showing the page's normal "invalid link" result.

In practice a link can get mangled quite easily, for example when it's copied out of a plain-text email together with a trailing period, or when an email client wraps or cuts it.

Affected code on `main`:

- Blazor Web App template: [`ResetPassword.razor`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWeb-CSharp/BlazorWebCSharp.1/Components/Account/Pages/ResetPassword.razor#L74), [`ConfirmEmail.razor`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWeb-CSharp/BlazorWebCSharp.1/Components/Account/Pages/ConfirmEmail.razor#L44), [`ConfirmEmailChange.razor`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWeb-CSharp/BlazorWebCSharp.1/Components/Account/Pages/ConfirmEmailChange.razor#L55)
- Identity UI V5 (same lines in V4): [`ResetPassword.cshtml.cs`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/Identity/UI/src/Areas/Identity/Pages/V5/Account/ResetPassword.cshtml.cs#L100), [`ConfirmEmail.cshtml.cs`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/Identity/UI/src/Areas/Identity/Pages/V5/Account/ConfirmEmail.cshtml.cs#L56), [`ConfirmEmailChange.cshtml.cs`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/Identity/UI/src/Areas/Identity/Pages/V5/Account/ConfirmEmailChange.cshtml.cs#L58)

These pages already handle the other kinds of bad links. `ResetPassword.razor` redirects to `Account/InvalidPasswordReset` when the code is missing, and the confirmation pages show "Error confirming your email." or "Error changing email." when the token is wrong. A code that isn't valid Base64Url just throws before it gets to those checks.

`MapIdentityApi` already catches the same exception in [`/confirmEmail`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/Identity/Core/src/IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L209-L216) and [`/resetPassword`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/f8bf4a7477a37fc09c9bdbe31b7938003b29b987/src/Identity/Core/src/IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs#L309-L317) and treats it like an invalid token.

### Expected Behavior

A malformed code should be handled the same way as a missing or invalid one: `ResetPassword` goes to the invalid link result (`Account/InvalidPasswordReset` in the template, the same `BadRequest` it returns for a missing code in Identity UI), and the confirmation pages show their existing error message.

For example, in the template's `ResetPassword.razor`:

```csharp
try
{
    Input.Code = Encoding.UTF8.GetString(WebEncoders.Base64UrlDecode(Code));
}
catch (FormatException)
{
    RedirectManager.RedirectTo("Account/InvalidPasswordReset");
}
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `dotnet new blazor -au Individual -o IdentityCodeRepro`, then `dotnet run` in that folder.
2. Open `/Account/ResetPassword?code=a`. The request fails with a 500 (`FormatException`). Opening `/Account/ResetPassword` without a code redirects to `/Account/InvalidPasswordReset` as expected.
3. Identity UI: `dotnet new webapp -au Individual -o IdentityUiCodeRepro`, `dotnet run`, open `/Identity/Account/ResetPassword?code=a`. Same 500.
4. For the confirmation pages, register a user, open the confirmation link and add a `.` at the end of the `code` value. The page fails with the same exception instead of showing "Error confirming your email."

I also ran the template's `ResetPassword.razor` and `ConfirmEmail.razor` from `main` (f8bf4a7) against the .NET 10.0.13 shared framework with an in-memory user store:

```text
GET /Account/ResetPassword                           302 -> /Account/InvalidPasswordReset
GET /Account/ResetPassword?code=YWJj                 200
GET /Account/ResetPassword?code=a                    500 (FormatException)
GET /Account/ConfirmEmail?userId=user-1&code=YWJj    200 ("Error confirming your email.")
GET /Account/ConfirmEmail?userId=user-1&code=YWJj.   500 (FormatException)
```

With the `try`/`catch` from Expected Behavior (and the same in `ConfirmEmail.razor`), the two malformed requests return 302 to `/Account/InvalidPasswordReset` and 200 with "Error confirming your email.", like the invalid ones.

### Exceptions (if any)

```text
System.FormatException: The input is not a valid Base-64 string as it contains a non-base 64 character, more than two padding characters, or an illegal character among the padding characters.
   at System.Buffers.Text.Base64Url.DecodeFromChars(ReadOnlySpan`1 source)
   at IdentityCodeRepro.Components.Account.Pages.ResetPassword.OnInitialized()
   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ComponentBase.RunInitAndSetParametersAsync()
```

### .NET Version

10.0.113 (also present on main, f8bf4a7)

### Anything else?

This is different from #40203, which was about how the code is generated and encoded. Here the link itself is malformed.

I'd be happy to open a PR that handles this in the Blazor template and in both Identity UI versions, with tests. :)

# Fix Blazor activity route correlation for per-page interactivity

## Description

Fixes missing route correlation on Blazor event activities when using per-page interactivity. Restores the aspnetcore.components.route tag and link to the corresponding navigation activity. Addresses dotnet/aspnetcore#64554 without changing public APIs or rendering, navigation, and event-handler semantics.

## Root Cause

Blazor stores navigation activity context in a renderer-local activity-link store. Per-page navigation runs in the static SSR renderer, while component events execute in a separate interactive renderer. The navigation context was not transferred, leaving event activities without route correlation while circuit correlation remained available.

## Solution

Transfer navigation activity context and route tags through the existing persistent-state infrastructure. Restore context during interactive renderer initialization and refresh it after enhanced navigation. Preserve live interactive Router context and circuit links, while clearing stale route context and avoiding payloads when no listener exists.

## Test Coverage

- Unit tests cover restoration, context round trips, stale-state clearing, Router precedence, scope isolation, and WebAssembly lifetimes.
- Browser tests cover Server, WebAssembly, and Auto initialization, prerendering options, enhanced navigation, and interactive Router controls.

Fixes #64554

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Return non-cacheable 404s when a manifest asset disappears.

## Description

When a file referenced by a static-assets manifest disappears, `StaticAssetsInvoker` catches `FileNotFoundException` and clears the response. Clearing resets it to an empty 200 response. A browser can cache that response and later reuse it for a fingerprinted Blazor boot resource.

- Return 404 with `Cache-Control: no-store` after clearing the missing-file response, and log the missing asset.
- In the development runtime handler, check that the source file exists before reading its length. Otherwise the request can throw before the invoker handles the missing asset.
- Add eight HTTP integration cases covering development/runtime patching and production behavior, compressed and uncompressed responses, and removal before or after a successful request. They check the missing response and successful serving after restoration.
- Preserve existing caching of healthy assets. This does not evict already-poisoned browser caches; loader recovery is implemented separately in dotnet/runtime#136527.

### Validation

Commands were run from the repository root after `. .\activate.ps1`.

```powershell
dotnet test .\src\StaticAssets\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticAssets.Tests.csproj -c Debug -bl /p:UseIisNativeAssets=false /p:RunAnalyzers=false --filter FullyQualifiedName~MissingAssetReturnsNonCacheableNotFound
```

Before the fix: **8 failed, 0 passed, 0 skipped**. The four production cases returned an empty 200 instead of 404; the four development cases threw `FileNotFoundException` while reading the missing file's length.

```powershell
dotnet test .\src\StaticAssets\test\Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticAssets.Tests.csproj -c Debug -bl /p:UseIisNativeAssets=false /p:RunAnalyzers=false --filter FullyQualifiedName~StaticAssetsIntegrationTests
```

After the fix: **70 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, including all eight new cases.

Analyzers were temporarily disabled on the command line with the author's authorization because the unmodified dependency projects fail public-API analyzers locally. No analyzer suppression or build workaround is included in this PR. No browser E2E tests were run for this server-only change; the regression is exercised at the real HTTP static-asset endpoint via TestServer.

Contributes to dotnet/aspnetcore#69488; this server-side prevention change does not by itself resolve existing poisoned browser caches.

> This PR was generated with GitHub Copilot and reviewed and validated in a local coding session.

Issues.Title: Fix an Issue of dispose a component's JS complement in a Blazor Web App using mixed render modes
Issues.Body:
### Description

- Issue disposing a component's JS complement in a Blazor Web App using mixed render modes.

### Root cause

- The issue is a lifetime mismatch between DOM removal and asynchronous component disposal.
- During enhanced navigation:
- The previous page’s interactive root is detached from the document.
- .NET starts disposing the root and its descendants.
- A component’s asynchronous disposer can pause at an incomplete await.
- The renderer processes removal and acknowledges the root-update batch before that asynchronous disposal finishes.
- When the disposer resumes and passes its original ElementReference to JS, the element is no longer discoverable through document.querySelector.
- The acknowledgement timing is visible in WebAssemblyRenderer: root removal is followed by the update-completion notification, without waiting for every asynchronous disposer.

### Fix

- Retain captured DOM elements when enhanced navigation removes a root component, keeping its ElementReference usable until asynchronous disposal finishes.
- Track pending disposal for the root and its descendants.
- Release references on actual disposal completion, not the earlier removal acknowledgement.
- Replay completion notifications after Server reconnect; clear retained state on permanent teardown.

### Test Case 

- Verified: Web.JS builds pass, 24 renderer tests pass, and both gated browser cases fail without the fix and pass with it.

Issues.Title: Identity API /manage/2fa ignores IdentityResult from SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The Identity API `POST /manage/2fa` endpoint ignores the `IdentityResult` returned by `UserManager.SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync`. When that update fails (for example with an optimistic concurrency failure), the endpoint continues as though the change was applied and returns a success response.

## What is wrong

* `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` returns an `IdentityResult` that reports store update failures (such as `ConcurrencyFailure`) rather than throwing. The endpoint awaits it and discards the result.
* The response therefore does not reliably reflect whether two-factor authentication was actually enabled or disabled. Subsequent steps (shared key reset, recovery code generation) also run against a state that may not have been persisted.
* Every other mutating endpoint in the same file checks `result.Succeeded` and returns `CreateValidationProblem(result)`; this endpoint is inconsistent with that pattern.
* Concurrent updates to the same user record (for example, other operations that update the user row such as failed sign-in bookkeeping) can make the update fail with a concurrency result, so this is reachable in normal operation.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* Correctness: callers cannot distinguish a persisted change from a rejected one, and a security-relevant setting (2FA enabled/disabled) can end up different from what the client was told.
* Hardening: security-sensitive state transitions should be fail-closed and report failure to the caller so clients can retry or surface an error.

## Affected code

* src/Identity/Core/src/IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs:532 - `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(user, true)` result ignored
* src/Identity/Core/src/IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs:536 - `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync(user, false)` result ignored
* src/Identity/Core/src/IdentityApiEndpointRouteBuilderExtensions.cs:539-542 - `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync` result in the same handler is also ignored (same class of issue; also again in the "no key yet" branch of the handler)

## Recommended fix

* Selected approach: capture the `IdentityResult` from both `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` calls and, when `!Succeeded`, return `CreateValidationProblem(result)`, matching the pattern already used by the passkey, password, and email endpoints. The handler's return type already includes `ValidationProblem`, so there is no public API or response-shape change for existing success paths.
* Alternatives considered:
  * Throwing on failure: rejected; it would surface as a 500 and diverges from the rest of the endpoints.
  * Retrying on concurrency failure inside the endpoint: rejected as larger behavior change; clients can retry on the validation problem.
* Follow-up consideration: apply the same check to `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync` calls in the handler; `GenerateNewTwoFactorRecoveryCodesAsync` returns a nullable enumerable instead of an `IdentityResult`, so its failure signal (`null`) needs a separate decision.
* Compatibility: previously silent failures now return HTTP 400 with an `application/problem+json` body keyed by the `IdentityError` code (for example `ConcurrencyFailure`). Successful requests are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] When `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` returns a failed `IdentityResult`, `/manage/2fa` returns a validation problem containing the error code, for both the enable and disable paths.
* [ ] A functional test in `src/Identity/test/Identity.FunctionalTests/MapIdentityApiTests.cs` uses a `UserManager` that returns `ConcurrencyFailure` from `SetTwoFactorEnabledAsync` and asserts both paths; the test fails without the fix and passes with it.
* [ ] Existing 2FA tests (`CanEnableAndLoginWithTwoFactor`, `CanLoginWithRecoveryCodeAndDisableTwoFactor`) continue to pass.
* [ ] Decision recorded for `ResetAuthenticatorKeyAsync` and recovery code generation handling.

Issues.Title: RemoteAuthenticationHandler ignores TicketReceivedContext.Fail() and proceeds to sign-in
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`RemoteAuthenticationHandler` ignores a failure result set through `TicketReceivedContext.Fail(...)` in the `TicketReceived` event. The handler continues to `SignInAsync` as if the event had completed normally, so the failure signal has no effect.

## What is wrong

* `RemoteAuthenticationContext<TOptions>.Fail(...)` is public API on the context passed to `OnTicketReceived`. It is documented only as "Indicates that authentication failed."
* After `Events.TicketReceived` runs, `HandleRequestCoreAsync` inspects only `Result.Handled` and `Result.Skipped`. `Result.Failure` is never examined, so a failed result falls through to sign-in and redirect.
* This is inconsistent with the same method's handling of `RemoteFailure`, which throws `AuthenticationFailureException` when `Result.Failure` is set, and with OpenID Connect `RemoteSignOut`, which also acts on `Result.Failure`.
* `TicketReceived` is invoked outside the `try/catch` that wraps `HandleRemoteAuthenticateAsync`, so only an exception thrown by user code, or `HandleResponse()` / `SkipHandler()`, currently prevents sign-in from this event.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* Correctness: a public API whose name and documentation say "authentication failed" is silently a no-op in this event. Apps that use it to enforce an application-level admission policy on an external identity get no enforcement.
* Hardening: the remote authentication handler is the boundary between an external identity provider and the local sign-in scheme. Failure signals raised by application code at that boundary should fail closed.
* Existing tests cover `SkipHandler()` and `HandleResponse()` for `OnTicketReceived`, but not `Fail(...)`, so the gap is not locked by any test.
* Applies to all remote schemes built on `RemoteAuthenticationHandler` (OAuth and derived providers, OpenID Connect, WS-Federation, and others). The same code is present on `main` and on `release/8.0`, `release/9.0`, and `release/10.0`.

## Affected code

* src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/RemoteAuthenticationHandler.cs:162-176 - result handling after `Events.TicketReceived`; no `Result.Failure` branch
* src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/RemoteAuthenticationHandler.cs:178 - `SignInAsync` reached when the result is a failure
* src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/RemoteAuthenticationHandler.cs:126-141 - existing `RemoteFailure` handling that already honors `Result.Failure`
* src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/Events/RemoteAuthenticationContext.cs:48-58 - `Fail(Exception)` and `Fail(string)` that set the failure result
* src/Security/Authentication/Core/src/Events/RemoteAuthenticationEvents.cs:21-39 - `OnTicketReceived` / `TicketReceived`

## Recommended fix

**Selected approach (servicing and main):** add a `Result.Failure` branch after the existing `Handled` and `Skipped` checks that throws `AuthenticationFailureException` before `SignInAsync` is called, mirroring the `RemoteFailure` handling. For example, use the message "An error was returned from the TicketReceived event." with `ticketContext.Result.Failure` as the inner exception. No public API change, so no `PublicAPI.*.txt` update or API review is needed.

**Alternatives considered:**

* Route the failure through `Events.RemoteFailure` so applications can render a custom error page. This gives a better experience but requires restructuring the shared failure block and the `Debug.Assert(ticket != null)` flow, changes event ordering and logging, and has a larger backport risk. It is reasonable as a follow-up on `main`.
* Leave behavior unchanged and document that `Fail(...)` is ignored in this event. Not chosen: the API reads as a rejection signal, and sibling handler paths honor it.
* Also honor `context.Success()` and other result shapes in this event. Out of scope for this fix.

**Compatibility and migration:**

* Apps that call `Fail(...)` in `OnTicketReceived` today and rely on it being ignored will start failing the remote login. This is a behavior change on servicing branches, so call it out in the PR description and release notes. Consider whether an `AppContext` opt-out switch is warranted, following precedent for similar servicing fixes.
* The supported ways to stop sign-in from this event remain `HandleResponse()` and `SkipHandler()`; their behavior is unchanged.
* The same hunk should backport cleanly to `release/8.0`, `release/9.0`, and `release/10.0`; the surrounding logic is identical on those branches.
* The existing XML documentation ("Indicates that authentication failed.") is accurate once the handler honors the failure, so no documentation change is required.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] Calling `Fail(...)` from `OnTicketReceived` prevents `SignInAsync` from being called, so no sign-in cookie is issued for the sign-in scheme.
* [ ] The failure surfaces as `AuthenticationFailureException` carrying the original failure as its inner exception.
* [ ] Regression tests in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.Test` cover an OAuth-derived handler (for example the Google tests) and OpenID Connect, next to the existing `OnTicketReceived_Skip_*` and `OnTicketReceived_Handled_*` tests. Each test fails without the fix for the expected reason and passes with it.
* [ ] `Handled` and `Skipped` behavior for `TicketReceived` is unchanged.
* [ ] The behavior change is noted in the PR description and servicing notes, and the opt-out decision is recorded.
* [ ] The fix is backported to `release/8.0`, `release/9.0`, and `release/10.0`.

Issues.Title: Migrate Blazor E2E tests to Components.Testing
Issues.Body:
## Summary

We introduced `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` (#65958, #66394, #68289) to provide a modern, Playwright based end-to-end testing infrastructure for Blazor applications. This issue tracks incrementally migrating our existing Selenium-based E2E test suite (`Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests`) to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing`, cleaning up our `testassets`, and evolving the library into a public package and agent skill that Blazor developers can use to test their own applications.

## Goals

1. **Incrementally migrate existing E2E tests to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing`:**
   - Replace legacy Selenium tests with readable, fast Playwright tests using `ServerFixture`, YARP proxy routing, and cross-process service overrides (following a developer experience similar to `WebApplicationFactory`).
   - Enable running E2E tests across multiple browsers and make it easy for developers and coding agents to run and filter E2E tests locally.
2. **Avoid test-logic flakiness by design:**
   - Tests migrated to the new infrastructure must be deterministic and not rely on arbitrary sleeps and polling.
   - Instead of one-off hacks in individual tests, we will build first-class synchronization primitives, lifecycle hooks, and readiness gates into the framework and testing library (for example, observing prerendered DOM state before interactive activation, waiting for Blazor runtime startup, enhanced navigation completion, or interactive handoff).
3. **Standardize framework test hooks for public consumption:**
   - As we migrate tests that currently rely on internal workarounds to inspect or gate framework state, replace those workarounds with clean, supported entry points and diagnostic channels.
   - Because `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` is intended to ship as a supported package for Blazor developers, the primitives we add should be designed for public consumption.
4. **Clean up and reorganize `testassets` and test structure:**
   - Re-evaluate and simplify the existing E2E `testassets` projects that have accumulated overlapping scenarios over time so they are easier to navigate and debug.
   - Support running selected test subsets across different hosting configurations (such as Server vs. WebAssembly) and isolated process configurations (such as different `AppContext` switches or Native AOT via #68289).
   - Improve CI and Helix execution partitioning (for example, attribute-driven test groups/traits and Helix job generation similar to `Wasm.Build.Tests` in `dotnet/runtime`).
5. **Better diagnostics, CI reliability, and developer/agent ergonomics:**
   - Leverage built-in Playwright tracing and structured diagnostics on failure.
   - Keep overall suite execution time low while separating genuine infrastructure failures (recoverable via selective test re-runs) from test-logic races.
   - Ship a reusable E2E testing skill and guidance so customers and agents can adopt `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Testing` in their own projects.

## Open Questions / Further Exploration

- How to best structure multi-environment and isolated `AppContext` test permutations in MSBuild and Helix.
- Whether and how to extend the testing model to cover `BlazorWebView` / Hybrid scenarios (WinForms, WPF, MAUI).
- Integration with CI selective retry / Test Monitor for transient machine or network failures.

Issues.Title: Remember me isPersistent understanding
Issues.Body:
This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)

Issues.Title: Cannot start a webapi on specific SSL port managed by IISExpress
Issues.Body:
A brand new netcore webapi 2.2 is created. 

Current launch settings:
```
{
  "$schema": "http://json.schemastore.org/launchsettings.json",
  "iisSettings": {
    "windowsAuthentication": false,
    "anonymousAuthentication": true,
    "iisExpress": {
      "applicationUrl": "http://localhost:62813",
      "sslPort": 44396

  },
```

The only way to start it on IIS Express is to keep 443 prefix (i.e. 44300, 44301, etc). 

Is this restriction by design as stated [here](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/content/problem/39430/changing-port-number-in-a-web-project-does-not-imm.html?childToView=43139#comment-43139)?

Issues.Title: System.Collections.Immutable dll being replace by Microsoft.Net.Compilers
Issues.Body:
I have referenced `system.collections.immutable.dll` from the nuget package and I also have the nuget package installed for `Microsoft.Net.Compilers`. Everything works fine in my local but when I push my code to bamboo, in the runtime I get `Could not load file or assembly 'System.Collections.Immutable, Version=1.2.3.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' or one of its dependencies. The located assembly's manifest definition does not match the assembly reference. (Exception from HRESULT: 0x80131040)`

When I checked logs on bamboo when it generates the artifacts, I can see that initially it copied the correct dll here:

`build    04-Apr-2019 03:20:33      Copying file from "E:\agt01\ENS-EB580-JOB1\Bin\Packages\System.Collections.Immutable.1.5.0\lib\netstandard1.0\System.Collections.Immutable.dll" to "E:\agt01\ENS-EB580-JOB1\Binaries\Release\\temp\Web\_PublishedWebsites\MyService\bin\System.Collections.Immutable.dll"`.

but then at some point, it replaced this dll with this: `build    04-Apr-2019 03:20:33      Copying file from "E:\agt01\ENS-EB580-JOB1\Bin\Packages\Microsoft.Net.Compilers.1.0.0\tools\System.Collections.Immutable.dll" to "E:\agt01\ENS-EB580-JOB1\Binaries\Release\\temp\Web\_PublishedWebsites\MyService\bin\System.Collections.Immutable.dll".`

How can I make sure that bamboo does not replace this dll and just uses it from the nuget package installed?

Issues.Title: Feedback: ensure that .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling only supported in VS 2017 and won't be supported in VS 2019
Issues.Body:
Apologize if my feedback may sound controversial or may spark a debate.

I need to be sure that the problem mentioned on this [page](https://github.com/aspnet/Tooling/blob/master/known-issues-vs2017.md#to-create-aspnet-core-10--11-projects-install-visual-studios-net-core-10---11-developer-tools-for-web-component) about .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling is installed when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project should not happen or should not be supported in VS 2019.

These are my main concerns:

1. VS 2019 is about to be released in around early 2019
2. ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 is not going to be supported anymore, based on [this page](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/master/microsoft-support.md).
3. Creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 will always install the .NET Core 1.0/1.1 web tooling, and this is not necessary when previous reason has reached the unsupported period and it's quite near or might be the same time of VS 2019 release.
4. Based on the problem mentioned above, VS 2017 has no "built in" tooling when creating new ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 project, but the external tooling may help. Therefore for those that still need to maintain ASP.NET Core 1.0/1.1 projects, we could use VS 2017 as long as the VS 2017 is still in support lifecycle or in mainstream support lifecycle.

I welcome feedback 🙂
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Feedback: ensure that .NET Core 1.0/1.1 tooling only supported in VS 2017 and won't be supported in VS 2019" (#1078)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time" (#537)

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.FindByLoginAsync`
- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.RemoveLoginAsync`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

Issues.Body:
Automates creation of documentation tracking issues in `dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs` when breaking change issues are opened or labeled in this repository.

**New workflow:** `.github/workflows/create-docs-issue.yaml`

- Creates issue in docs repo with:
  - Title: `[Breaking Change] <original title>`

- Posts comment on source issue with link to docs issue

Multi-layer detection to handle race conditions and partial failures:
- Checks for existing bot comments in source issue
- Searches docs repo by title before creating

Separate try-catch blocks for each operation:
- Comment listing failures → proceed with search
- Search failures → proceed with creation (fail open to avoid missing docs)
- Comment posting failures → don't fail workflow (docs issue already created)
- Permission errors → explicit message about `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` requirement

Configure `DOCS_ISSUE_TOKEN` repository secret with `repo` scope for cross-repository issue creation. Falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` but will fail with clear error message.

Explicit minimal permissions: `issues: write`, `contents: read`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Deprecating WebHostBuilder,  IWebHost, and WebHost
Issues.Body:
### Description

`WebHostBuilder` was replaced by `HostBuilder` ([generic host](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder)) in 3.0 and we also added [`WebApplicationBuilder`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) in 6.0.

We are now marking `WebHostBuilder` as obsolete to encourage users to move on to the alternatives which is where future investments will occur, and we're also marking `IWebHost` and `WebHost` as deprecated to clean up other parts of the now obsolete web host story.

### Version

.NET 10 RC 1

### Previous behavior

```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

### New behavior

Using `WebHostBuilder` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR004**:
> warning ASPDEPR004: WebHostBuilder is deprecated in favor of HostBuilder and WebApplicationBuilder. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/004.

Using `IWebHost` or `WebHost` will produce a compiler warning with diagnostic ID **ASPDEPR008**:
> warning ASPDEPR008: WebHost is obsolete. Use HostBuilder or WebApplicationBuilder instead. For more information, visit https://aka.ms/aspnet/deprecate/008.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [x] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [ ] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

We recommend the use of `HostBuilder` and `WebApplication` going forward over `WebHostBuilder` because they have all the features of `WebHostBuilder` and will be the focus of future investment.

### Recommended action

See https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/host/generic-host or https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/minimal-apis/webapplication for more details on the different hosting models. As well as [HostBuilder replaces WebHostBuilder](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/22-to-30#hostbuilder-replaces-webhostbuilder) and [Introducing WebApplication](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/migration/50-to-60#new-hosting-model) for migration guides.

Below is an example of converting `WebHostBuilder` to `HostBuilder`:

**Before**
```csharp
var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
    .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
    .UseStartup()
    .UseKestrel();
// Test code might use TestServer:
var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
```

**After**
```csharp
using var host = new HostBuilder()
    .ConfigureWebHost(webHostBuilder =>
    {
        webHostBuilder
            .UseTestServer() // If using TestServer
            .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
            .UseStartup()
            .UseKestrel();
    })
    .Build();
await host.StartAsync();

var testServer = host.GetTestServer();
```

Both Copilot and ChatGpt have given good results so far when asked to convert a WebHostBuilder example to use HostBuilder. Below is an example prompt:
<details>
<summary>Example AI Prompt</summary>

> Can you convert
>
> var hostBuilder = new WebHostBuilder()
>     .UseContentRoot(Directory.GetCurrentDirectory())
>     .UseStartup()
>     .UseKestrel();
> // Test code might use TestServer:
> var testServer = new TestServer(hostBuilder);
>
> to use HostBuilder.

</details>

### Affected APIs

`public class Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.WebHostBuilder`
`public interface Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.IWebHost`
`public static class Microsoft.AspNetCore.WebHost`

### Discussion

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/63480

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Exception diagnostics are suppressed when `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns true
Issues.Body:
### Description

The [ASP.NET Core exception handler middleware](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#exception-handler-page), `UseExceptionHandler()`, is responsible for catching and processing unhandled exceptions from ASP.NET Core requests.

In .NET 8, we introduced [`IExceptionHandler`](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/error-handling#iexceptionhandler). Implementations of `IExceptionHandler` are registered with dependency injection and invoked by the middleware. An implementation can return `true` from `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` to indicate that the exception has been handled. The middleware stops processing the exception once it has been handled.

In .NET 10, we're changing the default behavior so that the middleware no longer records diagnostics for exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

### Version

.NET 10 Preview 7

### Previous behavior

The exception handler middleware recorded diagnostics about exceptions handled by `IExceptionHandler`.

The exception diagnostics are:

- Logging `UnhandledException` to `ILogger`.
- Writing the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HandledException` event to `EventSource`.
- Adding the `error.type` tag to the `http.server.request.duration` metric.

### New behavior

If `IExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync` returns `true`, then exception diagnostics are no longer recorded by default.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

ASP.NET Core users have given feedback that the previous behavior was undesirable. Their `IExceptionHandler` implementation reported that the exception was handled, but the error handling middleware still recorded the error in the app's telemetry.

We are changing ASP.NET Core to follow the behavior expected by users by suppressing diagnostics when `IExceptionHandler` handles the exception. We're also adding configuration options to customize exception diagnostics behavior if needed.

### Recommended action

If you want handled exceptions to continue recording telemetry, you can use the new `ExceptionHandlerOptions.SuppressDiagnosticsCallback` option:

```cs
app.UseExceptionHandler(new ExceptionHandlerOptions
{
    SuppressDiagnosticsCallback = context => false;
});
```

The context passed to the callback includes information about the exception, the request, and whether the exception was handled. Returning `false` from the callback indicates that diagnostics shouldn't be suppressed. This restores the previous behavior.

### References

- Issue: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/54554
- PR: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/59074

### Affected APIs

- `UseExceptionHandler()`
- `IExceptionHandler`
